experience.task_summary: Repair three independent delivery-request failures: RecipientNames must return guest for null names, QuantityParser must return 0 for null/blank/invalid/negative quantities, and ItemSelector must return none for null/empty lists and invalid indexes, while preserving normal behavior and passing all 12 tests including FulfillmentService composition.
experience.root_cause: The component methods assumed valid input and directly called name.trim(), Integer.parseInt(text.trim()), or items.get(index), so null names, invalid or null quantities, and invalid or out-of-range indexes propagated exceptions instead of returning the required default values.
experience.solution: Add input guards to the three application source components: RecipientNames.normalize returns guest for null and otherwise keeps trim behavior; QuantityParser.parse returns 0 for null, blank/whitespace, non-numeric, or negative input and parses valid trimmed integers normally; ItemSelector.select returns none for null/empty lists, negative indexes, or indexes beyond the list size and otherwise returns the item. FulfillmentService required no change because its composition now yields guest|0|none for a fully invalid request.
applicability: Applies to the Java 17 Maven project using JUnit 5 and Maven Surefire with classes in package dev.selfevolving.benchmark.
RecipientNames.normalize must return guest for null input and preserve trim behavior for non-null input.
QuantityParser.parse must return 0 for null, blank/whitespace, non-numeric, or negative input, and must preserve normal parsing of valid trimmed integers.
ItemSelector.select must return none for null or empty lists, negative indexes, and indexes beyond the list size, and must return the selected item for valid indexes.
FulfillmentService.prepare composes the three components and must produce guest|0|none for a fully invalid request without changes to FulfillmentService.
Only application source files were changed; the test file was not changed.

issues.root_cause: RecipientNames.normalize directly dereferenced the input with name.trim(), so a null recipient name caused a NullPointerException.
issues.solution: Check for null and return guest; otherwise keep the existing trim behavior for non-null names.

issues.root_cause: QuantityParser.parse directly called Integer.parseInt(text.trim()), so null, blank/whitespace, and non-numeric text caused NumberFormatException; negative values were also not normalized to zero.
issues.solution: Return 0 for null, blank/whitespace, non-numeric, or negative input; parse valid trimmed integers normally and clamp negative parsed values to 0.

issues.root_cause: ItemSelector.select directly called items.get(index), so null/empty lists and negative or out-of-range indexes caused IndexOutOfBoundsException.
issues.solution: Return none for null/empty lists, negative indexes, and indexes beyond the list size; return the item normally for valid indexes.

experience.task_summary: Repair three input-normalization defects in the fulfillment helpers so missing or invalid inputs return safe sentinel values while normal inputs keep their existing behavior. After fixing recipient_name, parse_quantity, and select_item, the combined prepare call works and all 12 pytest tests pass.
experience.root_cause: The helpers directly dereference, convert, or index their inputs without validating missing values, non-numeric text, negative quantities, or index bounds, so invalid inputs raise AttributeError, ValueError/TypeError, or IndexError.
experience.solution: Add defensive handling in each helper: recipient_name returns "guest" for None or non-string names and still trims normal strings; parse_quantity catches ValueError/TypeError for blank, non-numeric, and None input, returns 0, and clamps negative values to 0; select_item returns "none" for negative, empty, or out-of-range indexes and returns the item for valid indexes. service.prepare remains unchanged because its combined behavior is fixed by hardening the three helpers.
applicability: Applies to the Python fulfillment helpers in fulfillment/names.py, fulfillment/quantities.py, fulfillment/items.py, and their use through fulfillment/service.py.
recipient_name: return "guest" when name is None or not a string; normal string names should still be stripped.
parse_quantity: return 0 for blank strings, non-numeric text, None, and negative quantities; valid numeric strings, including whitespace-wrapped values such as " 3 ", should return the integer value.
select_item: return "none" for empty collections, indexes >= len(items), and negative indexes; valid non-negative in-range indexes should return the selected item.
Combined prepare contract: after fixes, prepare(None, "bad", [], 2) should return "guest|0|none".

issues.root_cause: recipient_name calls name.strip() without checking for None or non-string input, so a missing recipient raises AttributeError.
issues.solution: Return "guest" when name is None or not a string; otherwise strip and return the normal string name.

issues.root_cause: parse_quantity calls int(text) directly, so blank or non-numeric text raises ValueError, None raises TypeError, and negative values are returned unchanged.
issues.solution: Normalize blank, non-numeric, and None input to 0 by catching ValueError/TypeError, and clamp negative parsed values to 0 while preserving valid numeric parsing.

issues.root_cause: select_item indexes directly into items without checking collection length or rejecting negative indexes, so empty or out-of-range indexes raise IndexError and negative indexes select from the end.
issues.solution: Return "none" for negative indexes, empty collections, or indexes >= len(items); otherwise return items[index].
